text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS

-- Under a framework agreement signed in Hanoi on Friday, France's Atomic Energy Agency (CEA) will help Vietnam produce its own nuclear energy within 15 years. French assistance will include nuclear physics and technology, production of isotopes, safety and protection against radiation and access to computer data.

-- The government does not think the current trade deficit will pose any problem to national economic development, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday. The trade deficit in the first eight months of the year was $3.246 billion.
-- The vice-chairman of the National Assembly Phung Van Tuu last Friday received a delegation from the culture committee of the French Senate.
-- The first development management course to improve management expertise within ministries began last week.

-- The President of the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA) Huguette Labelle began a three-day visit to Vietnam on Sunday. CIDA provides Vietnam with $12.75 million each year for information technology, environmental management, economic and administrative reform, financial management and rural finance projects.

-- More than 200 fake brand-name goods are on display at the Fake vs. Real Goods Fair '96 which opened on Saturday in Ho Chi Minh City. The imitation goods were collected by police and related organisations in Ho Chi Minh City and nearby provinces. - - - -
LE COURRIER DU VIETNAM
-- The prime minister has authorised Ho Chi Minh City to create a state investment fund of 500 billion dong ($45.37 million) for urban development.
-- The Hanoi People's Committee has decreed that from October 1, rollerskating in the streets will be banned to ensure traffic security.

-- The Ministry of Culture and Information decreed that from September 1, and until further notice, licences for satellite dishes would be restricted to diplomats, international organisations and accredited foreign news agencies in Hanoi.
-- Do Phuong, General Director of the Vietnam News Agency, and Associated Press President Louis Boccardi agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
-- Vietnam's soccer team beat Indonesia by three goals to two in Singapore on Sunday, taking third place in Southeast Asia's Tiger Cup. - - - -
NHAN DAN
-- A government decree on rail and water transport has come into effect in the country's northeast provinces of Quang Ninh, Thai Binh, Hai Hung and Hai phong city.
-- Vietnam has made ODA utilization in transport projects effective. Twenty-six projects with total capital of $1.283 billion, of which 85 percent was from ODA sources, are now under construction.
-- A $36.5-million factory to manufacture Samsung electronic products started operation in Ho Chi Minh City last week. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN
-- Floods killed eight people in coastal Ha Tinh province. The water level of rivers in the Mekong delta has started rising.
-- A prize for the best piece of writing about Fidel Castro was won by a Vietnamese man. The competition was organised to mark the 70th birthday of the Cuban President. - - - -
HA NOI MOI
-- A labour union of the Daewoo-Hanel joint venture company has been established.
-- Hanoi Urban Environment company has launched a campaign to welcome the Liberation Day of the city.
-- A bank card payment asociation has been established in Vietnam.
